items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: The interviewee explains that 'Nishiyuu' is the name of a song ('So for example “Nishiyuu” on “Habitat” came — I wrote that...') and refers to it as a branch of the Cree tribe.

ctx.x: Have you ever had an experience — you wrote glowingly about people that you work with, the soloists and so forth. I wonder if you’ve ever had a semi-awkward experience where people were interpreting your music during their solos in a fashion that didn’t really ring for you, and as the composer have you had to say, “Could you consider a different approach to this?”

Yeah that happens all the time I think. I might, you know, if I write something new and I throw it down in front of the band, this is a large ensemble. It’s a little different than small ensemble. If I’m in a quartet I can freely go crazy with my thoughts with the band because there’s only three or four of them in the room with me. But when you get to the hierarchy of placing a big band together there’s like little leadership roles going on everywhere. Right? So lead trumpet players are different everywhere.…
Wow. I watched a video from Jazz Composers Present that you were on, and you were talking about I think the name of the song was “Leap” maybe part three.
